summary: Defines various options that change the default behavior of APEX's relaying mesh. The core of APEX offers best-effort delivery of application-layer datagrams, and these options alter that default. The protocol is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: Normal mail has simple rules, but you can pay for extras like tracking. These were the extras for APEX message delivery. The whole thing is historic.

questions: how can apex relaying behavior be changed
how can apex limit message delivery time
how are forwarding loops prevented in apex
subtitle: Advanced options for controlling message timing, queuing, and loop detection in APEX.

tldr.problem: The core APEX service is best-effort and immediate, but applications sometimes need to queue messages, limit delivery time, detect loops, or force new connections to replace old ones.
tldr.mechanism: Four new APEX options extend the core service: attachOverride forces new attachments to replace old ones, dataTiming lets applications request timing constraints and delivery reports, hold4Endpoint queues data for offline endpoints, and dataHopping detects forwarding loops.
tldr.outcome: These options demonstrated APEX's extensibility, but like APEX itself, the protocol never saw significant deployment and is now historic.

today: RFC 3342 is now Historic. These options represented the design philosophy of APEX: a simple core service with pluggable options for advanced features. However, APEX never achieved deployment, so these options remain unused.

sections.title: Four Options for Extending APEX
sections.content:
RFC 3340 defines the core APEX service as best-effort and immediate. This RFC adds four options to the service, each addressing a common application need. These options are registered with IANA and follow the option framework of RFC 3340 Section 5.

Each option is identified by name, carries optional content, specifies which APEX elements it appears in, and defines processing rules. Options can appear at different scopes: per-attach, per-data, per-originator, or per-recipient. Relays process options based on a targetHop attribute that indicates whether the option applies at the current relay (this), only at the final relay (final), or at all relays (all).
sections.plainLanguage: Options are like special stickers on a message that change how APEX handles it. Each option has its own rules about when relays process it.

sections.title: attachOverride: Replace Old Sessions
sections.content:
By default, APEX allows at most one application to attach as a given endpoint at any moment. The attachOverride option changes this behavior for a new attach request.

When this option is present and another application is already attached as the requested endpoint, APEX terminates the old attachment immediately and allows the new application to take over. The relay sends the old application a terminate message with code 556 and the text 'overridden'.

This is useful when an application crashes or restarts on a different device and needs to resume without waiting for the old session to time out. The tradeoff is that data destined for the old session may be misdelivered to the new session. Applications must be prepared to receive data with unrecognized transaction IDs and handle it gracefully.
sections.plainLanguage: Normally, if you attach as 'Fred' from your computer, nobody else can attach as Fred until you log out. With attachOverride, your phone can kick your computer off and take over Fred's inbox.

sections.title: dataTiming: Deadlines and Delivery Reports
sections.content:
The dataTiming option lets applications specify timing constraints and request status reports. It carries a dataTiming element with four attributes, all optional and defaulting to zero:

noLaterThan is a milliseconds deadline. If data cannot be delivered within this time, the relay discards it and optionally sends an error report. returnTrip is the deadline for a success report to return to the originator. reportAfter is a time after which the relay should send a status report if delivery has not occurred yet (even if the message will later be delivered). reportErrors is a boolean requesting error reports.

Because timing changes at each relay hop, the option must be processed at every hop (targetHop='all'). The originating application must set mustUnderstand='true' to ensure all relays understand the semantics.
sections.plainLanguage: You can say 'deliver this within 10 seconds' or 'tell me if it is not delivered after 5 seconds'. Relays count down the timer as they forward the message.

sections.title: hold4Endpoint: Queue for Offline Recipients
sections.content:
By default, APEX silently drops data if the recipient endpoint is not currently attached. The hold4Endpoint option changes this behavior: if the recipient is offline, the relay queues the data waiting for the application to attach.

This is useful for applications like instant messaging, where the sender wants to guarantee that the message is not lost just because the recipient is temporarily offline. Without a deadline (the dataTiming option's noLaterThan attribute), data can be queued indefinitely. Applications typically combine hold4Endpoint with dataTiming to bound how long a message is held.

The security note is important: unlimited queuing can facilitate denial-of-service attacks. Administrators should restrict this option or require accompanying timing constraints.
sections.plainLanguage: If Barney is offline and Fred sends him a message with this option, the relay saves it. When Barney comes back online, he gets the message. Without this option, the message is lost.

sections.title: dataHopping: Detect Forwarding Loops
sections.content:
The dataHopping option is APEX's analog to IP's time-to-live (TTL) mechanism. It carries a dataHopping element with attributes noMoreThan (a hop limit) and reportErrors (a boolean).

Each relay that processes this option decrements noMoreThan by one. If the value reaches zero or below, the relay discards the message and optionally sends an error report via the APEX report service. This prevents messages from looping indefinitely if there are misconfigured relay routes.

Like dataTiming, this option must be processed at every hop (targetHop='all') with mustUnderstand='true'.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine you set 'this message can bounce between relays at most 3 times'. Each relay counts down. If it reaches zero, the message is dropped to prevent endless looping.
